# Preparation

Load in data

# Create civic engagement attitudes
## Wave 1
### Factor analysis
```{r}
IC_df <- as.data.frame(T1civeng[[1]])
# view(IC_df)

# Sample size = 121 (has to be > 300)
psych::KMO(IC_df) 
# KMO = .77 (has to be > .5)
det(cor(IC_df, use = "complete.obs")) 
# Determinant = 0.1928592 (> 0.00001)
ltm:: rcor.test(IC_df, use = "complete.obs")
# Only positive correlations (as it should be)

corrplot(cor(IC_df, use="complete.obs"), tl.col='black', tl.cex=.75) 

Factors_w1 <- fa(IC_df, nfactors = 4, rotate = "none", fm = "minres")
Factors_w1
```
### Reliability analysis
```{r}
reliability <- psych::alpha(IC_df[, c("T1CIVICENG1","T1CIVICENG2","T1CIVICENG3","T1CIVICENG4")])
reliability
# Raw alpha = 0.8096448
# All r.drop are > .3

reliability$alpha.drop 
# Removing T1CIVICENG4 results in a small increase of the Cronbach's alpha (0.82 instead of 0.81)
```

### Make scale
```{r}
IC_df$missings <- rowSums(is.na(IC_df))

IC_df$ce_t1 <- ifelse(IC_df$missings <= 1, rowMeans(IC_df[,1:4]), NA)

# View(IC_df)
```

<br>

### Dichotomise
```{r}
# Civic attitudes are relatively positive, overall. There is no one who scores lower than 3. For the dichotomisation, I have decided to put the cut-off point at a score of 5, as this is the direct middle of the actually observed scores, and it is the mean score. 

IC_df$ce_t1_cat <- cut(IC_df$ce_t1,
                       breaks = c(0, 5, 7),
                       labels= c('neutral', 'positive'))
table(IC_df$ce_t1, IC_df$ce_t1_cat)
```

<br>

## Wave 2
### Factor analysis
```{r}
IC_df2 <- as.data.frame(T2civeng[[1]])
#View(IC_df2)

# Sample size = 121 (has to be > 300)
psych::KMO(IC_df2) 
# KMO = .81 (has to be > .5)
det(cor(IC_df2, use = "complete.obs")) 
# Determinant = 0.08336661 (> 0.00001)
rcor.test(IC_df2, use = "complete.obs")
# Only positive correlations (as it should be)

corrplot(cor(IC_df2, use="complete.obs"), tl.col='black', tl.cex=.75) 

Factors_w2 <- fa(IC_df2, nfactors = 4, rotate = "none", fm = "minres")
Factors_w2
```

### Reliability analysis
```{r}
reliability2 <- psych::alpha(IC_df2[, c("T2CIVICENG1","T2CIVICENG2","T2CIVICENG3","T2CIVICENG4")])
reliability2
# Raw alpha = 0.8848902
# All r.drop are > .3

reliability2$alpha.drop 
# Removing T1CIVICENG4 results in a small increase of the Cronbach's alpha (0.88 instead of 0.90)
```

### Make scale
```{r}
IC_df2$missings <- rowSums(is.na(IC_df2))

IC_df2$ce_t2 <- ifelse(IC_df2$missings <= 1, rowMeans(IC_df2[,1:4]), NA)

# View(IC_df2)
```

<br>

### Dichotomise
To use the scales for civic attitudes to calculate Moran's I, and to make plots showing different attitudes, the variable needs to be dichotomised.

```{r}
# Civic attitudes are relatively positive, overall. There is no one who scores lower than 3. For the dichotomisation, I have decided to put the cut-off point at a score of 5, as this is the direct middle of the actually observed scores, and it is the mean score. 
IC_df2$ce_t2_cat <- cut(IC_df2$ce_t2,
                       breaks = c(0, 5, 7),
                       labels= c('neutral', 'positive'))
table(IC_df2$ce_t2, IC_df2$ce_t2_cat)
```

<br>

## Reciprocity
```{r}
#Wave 1
hangingw1_nona <- na_if(hanging[[1]][[1]], 9)
rowhangingw1 <- rowSums(is.na(hangingw1_nona)) == nrow(hangingw1_nona)
colhangingw1 <- colSums(is.na(hangingw1_nona)) == ncol(hangingw1_nona)
hangingw1_nona[which(rowhangingw1) , ] <- 0

g_strong_t1 <- igraph:: graph_from_adjacency_matrix(hangingw1_nona, mode = "directed")

reciprocity(g_strong_t1, ignore.loops = TRUE, mode = c("default", "ratio"))
# 0.4708861

# Wave 2
hangingw2_nona <- na_if(hanging[[1]][[2]], 9)
rowhangingw2 <- rowSums(is.na(hangingw2_nona)) == nrow(hangingw2_nona)
colhangingw2 <- colSums(is.na(hangingw2_nona)) == ncol(hangingw2_nona)
hangingw2_nona[which(rowhangingw2) , ] <- 0

g_strong_t2 <- igraph:: graph_from_adjacency_matrix(hangingw2_nona, mode = "directed")

reciprocity(g_strong_t2, ignore.loops = TRUE, mode = c("default", "ratio"))
# 0.4444444
```

## Path length
```{r}
# Wave 1
print(mean_dis <- mean_distance(g_strong_t1))
mean((ego_size(g_strong_t1, order = mean_dis, mode = "out") - 1)/vcount(g_strong_t1))
# 0.2180862

print(mean_dis <- mean_distance(g_strong_t2))
# Wave 2
mean((ego_size(g_strong_t2, order = 7, mode = "out") - 1)/vcount(g_strong_t2))
# 0.1705485
```

<br>

## Segregation
I calculated Moran's I with row standardisation, because I assume that each node is influenced equally by its neighbourhood, as there is no theoretical reason to assume otherwise specifically for civic attitudes. 
```{r}
# Wave 1
geodistances <- geodist(netw1, count.paths = TRUE)
geodistances <- geodistances$gdist

weights1 <- geodistances == 1 #Means that only direct ties are taken into account for segregation
ape::Moran.I(IC_df$ce_t1, scaled = FALSE, weight = weights1, na.rm = TRUE)

# Moran's I t1: -0.01401314, p-value: 0.942139

# Wave 2
geodistances <- geodist(netw2, count.paths = TRUE)
geodistances <- geodistances$gdist

weights1 <- geodistances == 1 #Means that only direct ties are taken into account for segregation
ape::Moran.I(IC_df2$ce_t2, scaled = FALSE, weight = weights1, na.rm = TRUE)

#Moran's I t2: -0.0178618, p-value: 0.9171138
```

# Data visualisation
## Wave 1
Create an igraph object
```{r}
copy_strong_netw_t1 <- strong_netw_t1
copy_strong_netw_t1[is.na(copy_strong_netw_t1)] <- 0 

g_strong_t1 <- igraph:: graph_from_adjacency_matrix(copy_strong_netw_t1, mode = "directed")
```

<br>

### Node colours based on civil service attitudes
```{r}
colour <- ifelse(IC_df$ce_t1_cat=='neutral', "lightpink", "orchid4")
graph_CE_t1 <- simplify(g_strong_t1)

# layout <- layout_with_dh(graph_CE_t1)
layout <- readRDS("layout.rds")

V(graph_CE_t1)$size = igraph:: betweenness(graph_CE_t1, normalized = T, directed = T) * 50 + 5
plot_CE_t1 <- plot(graph_CE_t1,
     vertex.color = colour,
     vertex.frame.color = "gray",
     edge.curved = 0.2, 
     edge.arrow.size = 0.1,
     vertex.label = NA,
     layout = layout)
legend("topleft", c("neutral", "positive", "missing"), pch = 21, col = "#777777", pt.bg = c("lightpink", "orchid4", "white"), pt.cex = 2,
    cex = 0.8, bty = "n", ncol = 1)
```

# RSiena
Putting the behavioural data in a matrix
```{r}
IC_df <- IC_df %>% 
  rownames_to_column(var = "id") 

IC_df2 <- IC_df2 %>% 
  rownames_to_column(var = "id") 

IC_df <- left_join(IC_df, IC_df2, by=c("id"))

behy <- IC_df %>% 
  dplyr::select("ce_t1", "ce_t2") %>% 
  as.matrix()
```
